title: IVE Overlay Schema
description: Single schema for any overlay, regardless of target technology. It validates the ENVELOPE only: that the file carries an `overlay` with a schemaVersion and a list of targets, and that every target names a JSONPath. WHAT EACH TARGET WRITES IS NOT VALIDATED HERE - that is the job of the `technology.yaml` descriptor of the namespace being written to, checked by the generator (validateOverlayValues) and drawn by the IDE from the same source. This schema used to carry if/then content rules for three namespaces (java, trigger, generation) as well, and they were removed on purpose: they covered an arbitrary 3 of the 9 namespaces that exist, they matched only ONE of the two valid ways to write a target (a target ending in the namespace, never a target whose content nests `extensions.<ns>`, which this project uses too), they had to be edited twice for every change - and they did drift, in both directions - and they ship on a different clock than the descriptors, which travel with the templates. One authority, covering every namespace and both target forms, beats two that disagree.

targets.description: Can be empty. An overlay that overrides nothing yet is a legitimate state - it is exactly what the IDE writes when someone creates one - and `minItems: 1` made that freshly created file fail validation before it could be filled in.

description.description: Descripción breve de para qué sirve este overlay - opcional, solo documentación.

target.description: JSONPath-style target, e.g. '$.extensions.java' or '$.flows.X.extensions.trigger'. It can also name the element alone ('$.intents.AddPet') and nest the namespaces under `extensions` in the entry's own content - both forms are valid and both are used.

overlayTarget.description: `additionalProperties` stays open on purpose: what a target writes belongs to the namespace it addresses, and that is declared in that technology's `technology.yaml`, not here.
